text:
Contributing Use Python 3.10–3.14 and Poetry 2: Update dependencies using `poetry lock`, never by editing the lockfile.
Douki docstrings must be synchronized and idempotent: The Makim groups, hooks, and release configuration are adapted from
[Douki](https://github.com/arxlang/douki), commit
`f77adee49546d4ea8e95ced671d470379c5bd741`.
The BSD license and upstream attribution are retained. Documentation is built
with DoukiMD. Publication is never triggered by pull requests. Publish the documentation After merging documentation changes, run the **Documentation** workflow
manually from upstream `main`. It builds the site and publishes the
`documentation` artifact to the `gh-pages` branch. Push and pull-request
runs only build and validate the documentation. After the first manual run creates `gh-pages`, configure **Settings → Pages**
to **Deploy from a branch**, selecting `gh-pages` and **/ (root)**.
The publishing action adds `.nojekyll` for the generated static site.

text:
Authoring and configuration Run `doukimd build --config doukimd.yaml` or `doukimd check`. The latter
compiles and validates without writing output. Paths are relative to the
configuration file; directory traversal and paths escaping the project are
rejected. See the runnable project under `examples/basic`. Markdown and metadata Pages under `docs/` become HTML at the same relative path. Optional YAML
front matter accepts `title`, `render` (`markdown` or `jinja`), and `meta`.
Unknown keys, duplicate keys, invalid types, and malformed YAML are errors. Enable Jinja with `render: jinja`. Templates receive `site`, `project`,
`page`, `data`, `api`, `plugins`, and `build`. Project configuration and
front matter remain literal YAML. Content is rendered once, before Markdown
parsing. Values returned by templates are not evaluated again. Content includes come from `includes/`. Use the `md_text` filter when
inserting a plain string into Markdown. Jinja syntax inside code fences is
still evaluated on templated pages: use Jinja raw blocks for literal examples.
Docstring prose is parsed as Markdown and never evaluated as Jinja. The dialect includes CommonMark, tables, footnotes, API blocks, and API
references. Raw HTML is disabled in content. Python code highlighting uses
Pygments; unknown languages fall back to plain text. Configuration Required settings are `site.title` and `project.name`. Defaults are
`schema_version: 1`, `docs_dir: docs`, `output_dir: build`, and
`includes_dir: includes`. Data is a mapping of names to YAML mapping files.
`project.version` is optional. `api.generate_pages` defaults to true. An API source has `language: python`, a project-relative `root`, and
`modules` containing import paths. Configured modules and their declared
submodules, classes, and functions are collected statically. Included public
declarations require valid Douki docstrings. Explicit Douki visibility and
atpublic decorators control visibility; underscores do not imply privacy.
Literal `__all__` limits module members. Explicit re-exports and exported
standalone attributes are rejected in this version. API blocks and references API blocks accept `members: none` or `members: public` and boolean
`show_source`. The latter displays a source location, not a repository link.
`{@api python:example.add}` links to the canonical generated page.
Unknown symbols and references without a generated destination fail the build. Generated pages live at `api/python/<qualified-name>.html`. Duplicate routes
are errors; authored overrides and canonical aliases are not implemented.
API directives inside docstrings are rejected. Links and output Relative Markdown links are rewritten to HTML and checked after all pages
and heading anchors are known. Duplicate heading anchors get stable numeric
suffixes. Local images and downloadable files must be under `docs/assets/`.
External and site-root links are not fetched or checked. Output includes HTML, CSS, `search.json`, `symbols.json`, and a versioned
build manifest. Search data is emitted; the bundled theme does not yet include
an interactive search UI. No generated Markdown is written into source. DoukiMD replaces an existing output directory only when its manifest identifies
it as a managed build. A failed compilation preserves the previous output.
The output directory must not overlap documentation, source, includes, theme,
or configured data inputs. Themes and plugins Set `theme.directory` to a local directory containing `page.html` to override
the bundled HTML template. Themes receive the content context plus
`content`, `navigation`, and `stylesheet`. HTML autoescaping is enabled;
only the engine-rendered content should use Jinja's `safe` filter. Explicitly enabled `plugins` are loaded from the `doukimd.plugins` Python
entry-point group. Each entry point exposes an object with a
`@doukimd.plugins.hookimpl` method named `doukimd_context(config)` returning
a JSON-compatible mapping. Its values appear under `plugins.<plugin-name>`.
Configuration order defines invocation order. Missing plugins, unsupported
hooks, and invalid results fail the build. Plugins run trusted Python code. Initial boundaries Arx collection, inherited members, dynamic Python APIs, overload sets,
automatic repository source links, incremental builds, a preview server, and
cross-project inventories are follow-up work. Arx configuration is rejected
until an adapter can consume retained frontend docstrings.
